title: Ordinary henselization commutes with a local quotient
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative local ring, let $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ be an ideal, and let $R^h$ be the ordinary henselization of $R$ [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime]. Then the quotient $R^h/IR^h$ is an ordinary henselization of the local ring $R/I$; in particular, the canonical map $R^h\to R^h/IR^h$ is local and surjective and identifies the structure map from $R/I$ with the quotient of the structure map from $R$.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 05WQ, Lemma quotient-henselization (lines 43616--43624): if $R$ is local with henselization $R^h$ and $I\subset\mathfrak m_R$, then $R^h/IR^h$ is the henselization of $R/I$.

proof.text: The quotient map R\to R/I makes R/I a cyclic R-module, hence a finite module; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-map-quasi-finite] therefore supplies the finite-type and quasi-finite-at-\mathfrak q hypotheses for [lem-trf-henselization-quasi-finite-ring], with A=R, B=R/I, \mathfrak p=\mathfrak m, and \mathfrak q=\mathfrak m/I. Since R and R/I are local, their localizations at these maximal primes are themselves. The tensor product R^h\otimes_R(R/I) identifies with R^h/IR^h, and the prime corresponding to \mathfrak q is the maximal ideal, so the localization in the cited lemma is this quotient. Its conclusion is therefore that R^h/IR^h is the ordinary henselization of R/I.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 05WQ, Lemma quotient-henselization (lines 43616--43624), explicitly as the special case of Tag 05WR

proof.text: The quotient map R^h to R^h/IR^h is surjective by the definition of an ideal quotient. The structure map R to R^h is local, so IR^h is contained in the maximal ideal of the local ring R^h; consequently the quotient map R^h to R^h/IR^h is local. Because I maps to zero under the composite R to R^h to R^h/IR^h, that composite factors canonically through R/I, giving exactly the stated compatibility of structure maps.
